assets.title: Cable-stayed bridge: two H-pylons, stays to the edge girders

provenance.basis: Illustrative archetype for visual explanation, not a reconstruction of a specific bridge and not an engineering design: two concrete H-pylons with a strut below the stay anchorages, straight stays in a vertical plane above each edge girder, a segmental deck; no anchorages. Proportions chosen for legibility on the 72 m site (flattest stay about 29 degrees).

references.title: Steel Bridge Design Handbook: Selecting the Right Bridge Type (FHWA-IF-12-052, vol. 5), 2.5 and 4.4
references.excerpt: The stay cables are inclined from the supporting towers to edge girders at or below the deck elevation.

assets.title: Steel cantilever through truss with a suspended span

provenance.basis: Illustrative archetype for visual explanation, not a reconstruction of a specific bridge and not an engineering design: anchor arms on the abutments and main piers, cantilever arms projecting from the piers, a suspended span between the arm tips; deepest over the piers. Proportions chosen for legibility on the 72 m site.

references.title: A Context for Common Historic Bridge Types (NCHRP 25-25, Task 15), 3.1 and 3.7
references.excerpt: A cantilevered truss bridge consists of anchor arms supported by piers, and a suspended span that is supported by the anchor arms.

assets.title: Steel pony truss bridge, Pratt web, 2 spans

provenance.basis: Illustrative archetype for visual explanation: proportions chosen for legibility at a common 24 m site; not a reconstruction of a specific bridge and not an engineering design. Parallel-chord pony truss (no top bracing below 4.5 m depth). Not structurally certified.

references.title: Truss bridge (Wikipedia)
references.excerpt: A Pratt truss includes vertical members and diagonals that slope down towards the center, the opposite of the Howe truss.

assets.title: Steel pony truss bridge, Warren web, 2 spans

provenance.basis: Illustrative archetype for visual explanation: proportions chosen for legibility at a common 24 m site; not a reconstruction of a specific bridge and not an engineering design. Same frame as bridge_steel_truss_pratt_01; Warren web with isosceles (not equilateral) triangles so both patterns share chords and nodes.

references.title: Truss bridge (Wikipedia)
references.excerpt: forming alternately inverted equilateral triangle-shaped spaces along its length ... with no vertical elements

assets.title: Stone arch bridge, 5 semicircular arches

assets.title: Suspension bridge: two towers, main cables, hangers, stiffening trusses

provenance.basis: Illustrative archetype for visual explanation, not a reconstruction of a specific bridge and not an engineering design: main cables at the outer edges draped over two towers and anchored in blocks on the banks, vertical hangers to the ends of transverse floor beams, a stiffening truss under each deck edge. Proportions chosen for legibility on the 72 m site.

references.title: Steel Bridge Design Handbook: Selecting the Right Bridge Type (FHWA-IF-12-052, vol. 5), 2.6
references.excerpt: The main cables typically are located at the outside edges of the bridge and are draped over the towers where they rest in saddles.

assets.title: District of 93 platforms in a sheltered bay (Design C)

provenance.basis: Illustrative archetype for projects/floating-city-design-challenge (scenario SCN_FLOATCITY_COASTAL_01); not an engineering design. Design C: 93 platforms of 60 m with three-storey buildings (draft 2.917 m from district_C); 66 home platforms inside, 27 service platforms on the seaward row and flanks; link-spans, piles in the shallow rows, conceptual mooring lines on the deep ring, a breakwater on the open side, utility spines (power, water, wastewater), boat landings, emergency routes. The link-spans are 25 m long (shore_gap_m), the bridge length of link_span.25_m_bridge in results.json.

assets.title: The same district towed out to open sea (counterfactual)

Three cables and pipes (power, water, wastewater) run 700 m along the seabed toward a shore beyond the frame (not routed or sized).

assets.title: Floating neighbourhood with piles and mooring lines (the story swaps one for the other)

assets.title: Floating platform A (40 x 40 m concrete pontoon, low-rise homes)

provenance.basis: Illustrative archetype of Design A in projects/floating-city-design-challenge (scenario SCN_FLOATCITY_COASTAL_01): an idealised concrete box pontoon with three-storey homes at its calculated draft (draft_m 2.958, analysis/results.json design_A.mid). The story's fourth storey and deeper hull are shown on floating_platform_a_section_01 and floating_platform_a_story_01. Not an engineering design; wall and slab thicknesses only serve the mass estimate.

assets.title: Floating platform A, section through the middle

provenance.basis: Illustrative archetype of Design A in projects/floating-city-design-challenge (scenario SCN_FLOATCITY_COASTAL_01): an idealised concrete box pontoon. draft_m 2.958 is the three-storey case of analysis/results.json (design_A.mid); the fourth storey and the 0.5 m hull extension are parts the story reveals, and their sinking and rising are applied as SEQUENCE MOVE steps with the offsets of analysis/results.json (storey_branch). Not an engineering design; wall and slab thicknesses only serve the mass estimate. The half in front of the cut, with the water and seabed in front of it, is built too so that the story can show the whole platform and then remove that half (B08); the section's marks (draft and freeboard dimensions, the outline of the water pushed aside, dashed reference levels) are drawing aids, not structure.

assets.title: Floating platform (Design A) with a 100 t test load and four neighbours

provenance.basis: Illustrative archetype of Design A in projects/floating-city-design-challenge (scenario SCN_FLOATCITY_COASTAL_01): an idealised concrete box pontoon. draft_m 2.958 is the three-storey case of analysis/results.json (design_A.mid); the fourth storey and the 0.5 m hull extension are parts the story reveals, and their sinking and rising are applied as SEQUENCE MOVE steps with the offsets of analysis/results.json (storey_branch). Not an engineering design; wall and slab thicknesses only serve the mass estimate. With a 100 t concrete block on the deck, which the story moves 15 m toward the edge (list_example in results.json: 100 t, 15 m, about 0.42 degrees). Four three-storey copies stand around a small basin (6 m gaps) for B12, where they arrive.
